This is my own result, written before any comparison with the steps' outputs. It is incomplete. The per-week reconciliation, the formula audit, the PNG check and the ATRI re-check did not finish, and I give no verdict.

**Step 1 (EIA data)**
- No Indiana series was found. In the saved EIA text, "Indiana" appears 0 times [S65, quoting the producer's earlier note]. I did not read EIA's full area list myself, so "no Indiana series" is not independently confirmed.
- The expected stand-in is the EIA Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 diesel retail series, ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG. I fetched its page at https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG&f=W on 2026-10-16 [S4].
- eia_weekly.csv uses this series ID and URL. The row I saw is 2025-10-06, 3.670 [S65].
- The latest week on the saved page is 2026-09-21 [S65, producer's note]. As of 2026-10-16, the Mondays 2026-09-28, 10-05 and 10-12 were not checked. A newer release may therefore exist, and the "latest" label is not confirmed.
- The 52 weeks ending 2026-09-21 would start on 2025-09-29. The CSV row dated 2025-10-06 is consistent with this. I did not count the rows or check the 7-day spacing myself.
- Three EIA prices were due to be re-checked against source (first, last and one random week). The saved page [S4] is the source. I did not complete the comparison, so none is confirmed.

**Step 2 (ATRI)**
- A snippet in the saved results says the truckload sector average reached $2.21 per mile in 2025. Its text about the overall industry average is cut off [S65].
- I could not confirm the ATRI total marginal cost per mile, the fuel cost per mile, the fuel share, the edition or the release date. These are unconfirmed.
- Fuel share should equal fuel cost per mile ÷ total cost per mile, both from the same edition.

**Step 3 (workbook)**
- Fleet gallons per week = 35 × 2,300 ÷ 6.2 = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 = 12,983.87.
- Worked example for 3.670 $/gal:
  - Surcharge = (3.670 − 1.25) ÷ 6.2 = 0.3903, which rounds to $0.39.
  - Fleet cost = 12,983.87 × 3.670 ≈ $47,650.81.
- Bands should be 41 rows, from $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps:
  - $3.00 gives 1.75 ÷ 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28.
  - $5.00 gives 3.75 ÷ 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60.
- I did not run the cell-by-cell comparison of 52 weeks against the workbook. I did not audit the formulas, the Inputs references, the cached values or the consecutive-Monday dates. I did not check the Summary average, high or low, or the stand-in flag.
- Files seen in the workspace: build/make_xlsx.py and recalc/diesel_fuel_surcharge.xlsx [S63].

**Step 4 (PNG)**
- I did not inspect the PNG for size, the 52 points, the axis labels, the title or the stand-in note. This is unconfirmed.
